posts.title: Soft sci-fi vs. hard sci-fi
posts.description: I selected five categories to try to decide the best type of science fiction: hard or soft ones. Yes, this is going to be another silly post. Indulge me while I try to convince you that one of these rises above the other! Ready? Fight!

posts.title: Age of Prosperity; Age of Stagnation: the setting of Childhood’s End
posts.description: Arthur C. Clarke’s classic Childhood’s End poses an interesting question: would world peace end science? Let’s put some perspective into the Age of Stagnation trope.

posts.title: The Machine Stops: an analysis on a timely dystopia
posts.description: The Machine Stops is cited as the first to feature a dystopic theme. It is a short story by E. M. Foster, better known for having written the classic A Passage to India. Foster is not often linked to science fiction, but The Machine Stops is regarded as one of the best of the genre. And I’m about to tell you why.
